title: Changing a CHECK in schema.sql does not reach existing indexes
trigger: when changing a CHECK constraint or column definition of an existing table in src/store/schema.sql (for example adding a lifecycle state)
behavior_delta: Add an explicit migration in migrate() (src/store/sqlite-index.js): detect the old definition in sqlite_master, drop that table's named indexes, rename the table, exec the schema, copy the rows back and drop the old table. Bumping INDEX_FORMAT alone does not help: rebuild() deletes rows but keeps the old table and its old CHECK, and copying rows keeps activation_count, which lives only in the index.
what: Add an explicit migration in migrate() (src/store/sqlite-index.js): detect the old definition in sqlite_master, drop that table's named indexes, rename the table, exec the schema, copy the rows back and drop the old table. Bumping INDEX_FORMAT alone does not help: rebuild() deletes rows but keeps the old table and its old CHECK, and copying rows keeps activation_count, which lives only in the index.
why: migrate() runs the schema with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, which never alters a table that already exists, so an index built by an earlier release keeps rejecting the new value at insert time. Found while planning the legacy state on 2026-09-24.
